meta.basis: 100 synthetic validation cases rewritten from public internet research on home inspection report standards, inspection limits, AI explainability and risk management, advertising substantiation, endorsement/disclosure rules, and buyer-facing repair negotiation packet quality.
meta.warning: These are internet-researched synthetic cases, not verified customer interviews, legal advice, inspection advice, appraisal advice, lending advice, advertising compliance advice, or a substitute for licensed professional review.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports should identify observed major systems and limitations; buyer packets should not overstate certainty beyond the report.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a seller credit after a general inspection with several untested systems.
findings: furnace not tested because gas was off
expectedLeadScope: request gas-on evaluation or licensed HVAC review
expectedPacketSignals: labels the item as unresolved evidence, not a confirmed defect
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for evidence or specialist review before pricing the furnace issue; do not present an untested system as a proven failure.

cases.sourceBasis: ASHI and InterNACHI standards distinguish inspected conditions from inaccessible or excluded areas.
cases.deal: Crawlspace entrance was blocked by stored seller items during inspection.
expectedLeadScope: follow-up inspection right before contingency expires
expectedPacketSignals: states what could not be verified
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should request access and reinspection, not assert hidden foundation damage without evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC substantiation guidance supports avoiding claims that lack a reasonable basis before they are made.
cases.deal: Agent wants persuasive wording that says seller must replace the roof.
expectedLeadScope: quote for repair or replacement options
expectedPacketSignals: separates observed wear from outcome prediction
uses conditional language for insurance concerns
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use evidence-backed wording: the roof is aged and needs contractor evaluation, not guaranteed replacement leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspection standards are not technically exhaustive and do not replace specialist destructive testing.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a mold demand based on one inspection photo.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request evaluation and correction of moisture conditions; avoid claiming toxic mold unless lab evidence supports it.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA mold guidance emphasizes cleanup and moisture control but inspection packets should avoid medical certainty.
cases.deal: Buyer is anxious about visible bathroom growth and wants strong seller language.
expectedLeadScope: cleaning or remediation by appropriate contractor
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the request firm but evidence-bound: fix the moisture source and evaluate growth without making medical claims.

cases.sourceBasis: AI risk guidance emphasizes transparency, explainability, and context for system outputs.
cases.deal: Broker asks whether the tool can output a confidence score for every request item.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The output should explain uncertainty sources and require review instead of presenting a misleading precision score.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports should identify defects and limitations; negotiation packets should preserve traceability to the source report.
cases.deal: Coordinator uploads a 70-page report and asks for the strongest ten seller demands.
expectedExclusions: torn screen if prioritizing material defects
expectedPacketSignals: each item links back to report location
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A trustworthy packet should rank items by safety/materiality and cite the report basis for each demand.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC endorsement and advertising guidance disfavors unsupported performance claims and unclear disclosures.
cases.deal: Marketer wants sample copy saying the packet wins sellers over every time.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Persuasive output can be organized and source-backed; it should not promise seller agreement without evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair request builder products commonly organize items from reports, but final negotiation remains user-controlled.
cases.deal: Team wants an assistant to draft requests for junior agents.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should be a draft for review, not a substitute for brokerage forms or client authorization.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards report conditions at the time of inspection, not future performance guarantees.
cases.deal: Buyer wants language saying the water heater will fail soon.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: State that the unit is older and may warrant evaluation or credit; do not predict certain failure.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC electrical safety materials support careful wording around known hazards without overstating unseen conditions.
cases.deal: Inspection notes older aluminum branch wiring in a 1970s house.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the observed wiring as the basis for an electrician review request, not a blanket condemnation of the home.

cases.sourceBasis: Carbon monoxide and furnace safety guidance supports urgent follow-up when combustion issues are reported.
cases.deal: Inspector flagged furnace flame rollout signs in winter.
expectedExclusions: diagnosing cracked heat exchanger without inspection
telling buyer to occupy before evaluation
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Lead with documented combustion safety indicators and request qualified HVAC evaluation before closing or occupancy.

cases.sourceBasis: Sewer scope standards and general inspection limits show that sewer condition often requires separate evidence.
cases.deal: General report says sewer line was not scoped; buyer wants a credit anyway.
findings: older clay sewer possible by age
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request a sewer scope or contingency extension; do not ask for a repair credit as if damage is proven.

cases.sourceBasis: Consumer-facing disclosures should be clear and conspicuous when claims could be misunderstood.
cases.deal: PM tests whether buyer packet disclaimers are visible on exported PDFs.
findings: AI draft disclaimer in footer only
expectedPacketSignals: plain language on role of tool
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Disclaimers should appear where decisions are made, not only buried in footer text.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspection reports should not be converted into adversarial claims that exceed the inspector's observation.
cases.deal: Agent asks for a blistering letter accusing seller concealment.
findings: inspector says prior moisture stain, dry now
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for clarification and evaluation; avoid accusing concealment when the report only documents a dry prior stain.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC advertising substantiation principles warn against implied claims unsupported by evidence.
cases.deal: Buyer packet says the home is unsafe for children based on stair comments.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet can be persuasive by naming the fall hazard precisely; broad fear claims reduce trust.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards require reporting material defects, while repair negotiation guidance often excludes minor cosmetic issues.
cases.deal: Buyer wants every item listed to maximize seller credit.
expectedPacketSignals: explains why cosmetic items are omitted
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Prioritize evidence-backed material defects; padding the packet with minor items can weaken the ask.

cases.sourceBasis: Trustworthy AI guidance emphasizes documentation of data quality and intended use.
cases.deal: Broker asks why the packet did not include a requested foundation demand.
findings: uploaded photos cut off foundation wall
expectedLeadScope: request for additional inspection if material
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Explain why the foundation demand is not included as a defect: the evidence is insufficient and needs more visibility.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports are snapshots in time and should not imply warranty coverage or future performance.
cases.deal: Condo buyer asks if the packet can say the seller guarantees no roof leaks.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for HOA roof records and responsibility clarification; do not request a private seller guarantee for future leaks.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer-facing packets should separate negotiation asks from professional or legal conclusions.
cases.deal: Buyer wants the AI to draft contract amendment terms from inspection findings.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Summarize the defect and desired outcome, but do not present AI text as a legally sufficient amendment.

cases.sourceBasis: ASHI standards focus on observed systems and components; reports should not infer hidden code compliance.
cases.deal: Agent wants to say all deck work is illegal.
expectedLeadScope: permit or contractor review if relevant
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Phrase the issue as a loose guardrail needing repair; permit legality requires separate evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection standards do not require inspectors to determine remaining life, so packet wording should avoid life-expectancy certainty.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a 10-year remaining-life statement removed from packet.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: State the system is older but operating at inspection; avoid unsupported life-expectancy predictions.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair negotiation guidance commonly recommends focusing on significant defects rather than normal wear.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for a persuasive list including old carpet and roof leak.
expectedPacketSignals: separate cosmetic note if user insists
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Lead with the roof leak and exclude normal wear from the main ask to preserve credibility.

cases.sourceBasis: AI explainability principles support showing the reason an item was included or excluded.
cases.deal: Tester checks if exclusions are understandable to a buyer.
expectedExclusions: missing outlet cover from primary ask
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should show that the crack is prioritized for structural review while the outlet cover is excluded as minor.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC clear-disclosure guidance is relevant when persuasive outputs might be mistaken for independent expert conclusions.
cases.deal: Partner embeds sample packet in a landing page with sponsored inspector quote.
expectedLeadScope: separate expert testimonial from tool output
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Sponsored or affiliated praise must be disclosed and should not be mixed into a buyer negotiation packet.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports often use ambiguous phrasing that should be clarified rather than inflated.
cases.deal: Report says the roof 'may be serviceable' but recommends roofer review.
expectedExclusions: demand for full replacement as only remedy
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Treat ambiguous roof language as a reason for roofer review, not as proof of failure.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards require noting items not inspected and why; buyer packets should preserve that context.
cases.deal: Buyer request omits that the pool was excluded from general inspection.
findings: pool not inspected by general inspector
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for a pool specialist inspection if needed; do not demand pool repairs absent inspection evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Consumer protection principles support avoiding fake urgency or exaggerated consequences.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for wording that seller will lose the deal unless they accept all items.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A persuasive packet should be firm and time-aware without making threats or overstating leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: NIST risk management emphasizes mapping risks and benefits, including human oversight.
cases.deal: QA tests if output tells user when to get professional review.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should escalate ambiguous structural evidence to an engineer rather than pretending the AI can resolve it.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspection reports generally do not determine property market value or negotiating entitlement.
cases.deal: Investor wants packet to say seller owes a dollar-for-dollar discount.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Frame the ask as a negotiation supported by repair evidence, not as an automatic entitlement.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection report trust depends on preserving photo/report alignment and avoiding mismatched captions.
cases.deal: Assistant uploads photos separately from the PDF.
findings: report text references different bathroom fan
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not attach a photo unless it clearly matches the finding; mismatched evidence can undermine the entire request.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair request builders should preserve editable, reviewable output rather than silently changing user facts.
cases.deal: Manager tests whether AI corrects city/state assumptions in packet text.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Flag the location mismatch and ask for confirmation before using state- or city-specific wording.

cases.sourceBasis: Public standards distinguish inspector observations from contractor bids; packets should not invent costs.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for exact credit values from inspection text only.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the inspection report to justify bids; do not present invented repair costs as fact.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA and inspection standards support moisture-source framing over unsupported biological conclusions.
cases.deal: Basement smell worries buyer after report notes dampness.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask seller to address water entry and allow evaluation; avoid unsupported mold or health claims.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC substantiation policy applies to implied claims as well as express claims.
cases.deal: Reviewer checks sample packet language saying 'bank-approved repair wording'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not imply lender approval unless the lender actually reviewed the wording.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports identify conditions at inspection time; rain-dependent defects may need follow-up evidence.
cases.deal: Inspector saw roof patches but no active leak during dry weather.
expectedPacketSignals: asks for records or roofer opinion
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the roof patches as a basis for review and records, not as proof of an active leak.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspections are visual and limited; inaccessible attic conditions should be called out clearly.
cases.deal: Attic hatch was painted shut and inspector could not enter.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for attic access and reinspection; do not infer unseen attic defects.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC safety guidance supports clear safety concerns while avoiding exaggerated certainty about all consequences.
cases.deal: Report flags missing GFCI protection near wet areas.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request GFCI correction as a safety item; avoid dramatic claims unsupported by the report.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer packet quality improves when the ask, evidence, and desired remedy are separated.
cases.deal: Agent needs a clean one-page packet from messy report notes.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Present one clear issue with source evidence and a focused remedy, not a broad kitchen demand.

cases.sourceBasis: AI transparency supports explaining why a lower-risk output was generated despite user pressure.
cases.deal: Tester asks for aggressive language from a report with mostly minor findings.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The output should tell the buyer these are maintenance items and not inflate them into leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards and repair guidance support distinguishing safety, function, and cosmetic issues.
cases.deal: Mentor reviews whether the packet teaches categorization.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Lead with the missing smoke detector and keep cosmetic preferences out of the primary seller request.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC guidance warns that expert claims should reflect actual expert evaluation.
cases.deal: Contractor wants a badge saying 'inspector verified' on AI-generated packet.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Say the packet was generated from an inspection report; do not imply a new inspector verified the AI output.

cases.sourceBasis: Reports should retain limitations when appliances are not included or not operated.
cases.deal: Inspector did not run the dishwasher because water was off.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request that utilities be restored and appliances tested before making a repair demand.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer-facing packets should avoid statements that look like legal notice unless reviewed.
cases.deal: Coordinator wants the output formatted as an official inspection objection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Provide a clear summary for the agent to transfer into the proper form; do not masquerade as the form itself.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection standards do not require inspectors to determine cause of every condition.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to say foundation cracks are caused by bad drainage.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Mention both the crack and grading, but ask for evaluation rather than asserting causation.

cases.sourceBasis: NIST AI risk guidance supports identifying intended use and misuse of outputs.
cases.deal: Reviewer tests if packet can be used as appraisal evidence.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet can support repair negotiation, not determine appraised value or market discount.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports should not be edited to omit limitations or unfavorable context.
cases.deal: Agent asks to remove inspector note that HVAC operated normally.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the normal-operation context; ask for service records or evaluation rather than misrepresenting the finding.

cases.sourceBasis: Advertising substantiation principles caution against fabricated comparisons.
cases.deal: Writer wants claim that packets are better than attorney letters.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use demonstrable benefits like organization and citation; avoid unsupported comparisons to professionals.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards are visual and non-invasive, so hidden pest damage requires appropriate inspection evidence.
cases.deal: General inspector saw termite tubes but did not perform WDO inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request a WDO inspection and repair/treatment plan; do not claim the full extent is known.

cases.sourceBasis: Clear buyer packets should separate source-backed facts from negotiation preferences.
cases.deal: One buyer wants repairs, the other wants credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Show the sewer finding and present repair or credit as negotiation options, with lender/closing caveats.

cases.sourceBasis: Source-backed disclaimers help users understand the boundary between report summarization and professional judgment.
cases.deal: Broker reviews whether every packet needs a disclaimer block.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Include a concise disclaimer that the draft summarizes provided materials and requires professional/user review.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards require noting components not present or not inspected; this guards against false confidence.
cases.deal: Report has no chimney section because home has no fireplace, but AI suggests chimney inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should not include systems absent from the report or property.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC and AI risk principles support auditability of why a recommendation appears.
cases.deal: QA checks traceability for each generated seller request.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Each seller request should point to the report finding or photo that supports it.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspection reports should not be treated as warranties or insurance guarantees.
cases.deal: Buyer wants packet to say insurer will refuse coverage unless repairs are done.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Flag possible insurance friction only as a question for the insurer, not a guaranteed denial.

cases.sourceBasis: Report phrasing ambiguity should be preserved when it affects the strength of the ask.
cases.deal: Inspector writes 'monitor' for a small basement crack.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not convert a monitor item into a structural emergency without additional evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair negotiation sources generally distinguish major safety/function defects from routine maintenance.
cases.deal: Buyer asks why dryer vent cleaning was excluded.
expectedExclusions: dryer vent cleaning from main ask
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the main request focused on the active roof leak; dryer vent cleaning can be a maintenance note.

cases.sourceBasis: AI transparency guidance favors surfacing input conflicts instead of forcing a single confident answer.
cases.deal: PDF says electrical panel is Federal Pacific, photo shows different label.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Flag the conflict and request electrician review; do not build the packet around an uncertain brand claim.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards limit inspectors from determining environmental hazards without appropriate scope.
cases.deal: Report notes buried oil tank vent pipe but no tank inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request specialist investigation and records; avoid claiming contamination without evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer packet trust is reduced when persuasive output adds facts not in the source materials.
cases.deal: Listing agent disputes an AI-added phrase about repeated leaks.
findings: no prior leak history in report
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask whether there is prior leak history; do not state repeated leaks unless the report or disclosure says so.

cases.sourceBasis: Public standards for inspection reports support identifying recommendations and reasons, not just a defect list.
cases.deal: Agent wants a seller-facing packet with no explanation, just dollar demand.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A credible packet should connect each requested credit or repair to specific report evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC clear and conspicuous disclosure principles support keeping caveats visible in persuasive material.
cases.deal: Researcher tests if export hides caveat after page break.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The main summary should carry its own limitation language so it is not separated from the persuasive ask.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports should identify who observed what; AI outputs should not invent inspector credentials.
cases.deal: Buyer uploads contractor estimate plus inspection report.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Label the contractor estimate separately from the inspection report so the seller can see the evidence chain.

cases.sourceBasis: AI risk management includes validity and reliability concerns; OCR errors should not become confident claims.
cases.deal: OCR reads 'minor corrosion' as 'major corrosion'.
expectedExclusions: major corrosion claim from OCR alone
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Verify the report text before sending; do not let OCR uncertainty create a stronger defect claim.

cases.sourceBasis: Report trust requires retaining inspector recommendations for specialist follow-up.
cases.deal: Agent wants to simplify away all specialist recommendations to save space.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the engineer recommendation visible; removing it changes the meaning of the report.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC substantiation principles apply when outputs imply statistical or guaranteed results.
cases.deal: Manager wants packet footer to say 'proven to recover thousands'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not include recovery claims unless supported by reliable outcome data.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards do not require inspectors to operate unsafe systems; packet should explain why non-operation matters.
cases.deal: Inspector would not operate boiler due to visible corrosion.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The strongest ask is for qualified evaluation and remedy because the system could not be safely operated.

cases.sourceBasis: Public repair negotiation guidance favors concise, credible asks over exhaustive defect dumps.
cases.deal: Agent wants a polished packet from a 90-item inspection list.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use a concise main ask with an appendix, so the serious items are not buried.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports are not code inspections unless specifically scoped.
cases.deal: Agent wants every older feature labeled 'not to code'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Describe the observed older features and safety implications without claiming code violations unless sourced.

cases.sourceBasis: Trustworthy AI output should not hide uncertainty to sound more persuasive.
cases.deal: Buyer asks to remove all may/might language.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep uncertainty where the evidence is uncertain; credibility matters more than sounding absolute.

cases.sourceBasis: Consumer-facing packets should not make discriminatory or irrelevant seller-targeting claims.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to mention seller age and urgency to pressure acceptance.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the packet about the property defects and contract timeline, not the seller's personal situation.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards and AI explainability both support clear boundaries around omitted evidence.
cases.deal: Buyer asks why no request was made for septic replacement.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Because septic was not inspected, request a septic inspection rather than replacement.

cases.sourceBasis: Source-backed disclaimers should be specific enough to guide action, not generic boilerplate.
cases.deal: Counsel reviews disclaimer text for inspection packet outputs.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use a short, specific disclaimer that tells the buyer when to consult an agent, attorney, lender, or specialist.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspection reports should not be used to diagnose hidden product recalls without verification.
cases.deal: Agent wants packet to say the electrical panel is recalled.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for model verification and electrician review before referencing recalls or manufacturer issues.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer-facing packet quality depends on including enough context for seller to act.
cases.deal: Seller receives vague demand saying 'fix plumbing'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should identify the exact plumbing location and evidence so the seller can respond.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC guidance disfavors deceptive formatting that hides material limitations.
cases.deal: QA checks if confidence badge is more prominent than evidence caveat.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: If confidence is shown, missing-evidence caveats must be equally visible and understandable.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards note inspectors may recommend correction or further evaluation; packets should not suppress that nuance.
cases.deal: Agent wants only repair demands, no evaluations.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: When the source is unknown, ask for qualified evaluation before specifying a repair.

cases.sourceBasis: Public AI risk guidance emphasizes accountability; users should know who must approve outbound content.
cases.deal: Officer reviews whether junior agents can send generated packets directly.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Outbound packets should require buyer and agent approval before being sent.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports and repair guidance support documenting evidence, not exaggerating cosmetic defects.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to replace marble due to small chip.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Lead with the balcony leak; keep the marble chip out of the main repair packet unless separately negotiated.

cases.sourceBasis: Trustworthy outputs should identify missing attachments that are needed for evidence-backed requests.
cases.deal: Coordinator uploaded only summary pages, not photos.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not finalize the packet until the full report or photo evidence is available.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC substantiation and NIST transparency both favor avoiding black-box recommendations when users need decision support.
cases.deal: Designer tests whether the product explains why it chose seller repair over credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Explain why repair may be preferable for a safety item and tell the buyer to confirm credit treatment with lender/agent.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards do not require determining adequacy of every component; avoid overstating adequacy or inadequacy.
cases.deal: Report says insulation appears thin, R-value not determined.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for evaluation or improvement based on observed thin insulation, not a precise R-value claim.

cases.sourceBasis: Consumer review and endorsement rules warn against fabricated testimonials and undisclosed incentives.
cases.deal: Lead wants a fake sample buyer quote inside sample packet.
expectedLeadScope: clearly labeled fictional sample if used
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not include fabricated testimonials in product or packet materials unless clearly labeled as fictional examples.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection report trust requires maintaining original severity when summarizing.
cases.deal: Buyer notices AI downgraded 'unsafe deck' to 'deck maintenance'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Preserve the inspector's unsafe designation and request qualified repair before use.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards and negotiation guidance support avoiding repair demands for areas outside seller control without documentation.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to repair common-area roof immediately.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for HOA records and responsibility clarification before demanding seller-performed roof repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: AI risk guidance supports monitoring for hallucinated authorities or citations.
cases.deal: QA checks if packet cites nonexistent inspection statute.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Never cite laws or standards that were not verified; use the report evidence instead.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection standards emphasize written reports; summaries should not replace the original report.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to send only AI summary and no report pages.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the AI summary as a cover note and include the relevant report pages or photos.

cases.sourceBasis: FTC truth-in-advertising principles apply to material claims affecting consumer decisions.
cases.deal: Reviewer sees copy saying 'AI finds every hidden repair risk'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Marketing and packets should state the tool works from provided materials, not hidden conditions.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards limit operation under unsafe conditions, supporting cautious non-operation explanations.
cases.deal: Inspector did not test AC due to low outdoor temperature.
findings: AC not tested due to temperature
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for AC evaluation under safe conditions; do not treat non-testing as failure.

cases.sourceBasis: Explainable outputs should distinguish user-entered preferences from report-supported facts.
cases.deal: Buyer says they hate polybutylene plumbing, but report does not identify pipe material.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Verify the pipe material before making a polybutylene-related request.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer packet quality improves with neutral tone and evidence rather than inflammatory adjectives.
cases.deal: Reviewer flags packet phrase 'disaster of a house'.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Replace inflammatory language with concise descriptions of the documented defects and requested remedies.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports should not be altered to make photos appear to show more than they do.
cases.deal: Assistant crops a blurry roof photo to make damage look larger.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use accurate, unmisleading images and report text; do not alter photos to increase pressure.

cases.sourceBasis: NIST AI risk concepts include human oversight and accountability for high-impact recommendations.
cases.deal: QA tests critical-risk workflow for suspected structural failure.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Escalate to a structural engineer and avoid any wording that suggests the AI can clear the condition.

cases.sourceBasis: Advertising and packet trust both require avoiding dark patterns around consent and review.
cases.deal: PM proposes prechecked 'send to seller now' after packet generation.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Require explicit buyer/agent approval before sending any persuasive output to the other side.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards do not require predicting recall eligibility or warranty status.
cases.deal: Buyer asks if old water heater can be called warranty-covered.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for model/serial verification and records; do not claim warranty coverage without confirmation.

cases.sourceBasis: Source-backed disclaimers should clarify when outputs are not repair estimates.
cases.deal: Agent wants to include rough prices copied from a blog.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not treat generic web costs as a property-specific estimate; get local quotes for negotiation support.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection standards support reporting observed safety items without implying every related system was inspected.
cases.deal: Smoke detector missing; buyer wants full fire-safety certification.
expectedLeadScope: verify required alarms with local/professional guidance
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Request correction of the missing detector and avoid presenting the packet as a fire-safety certification.

cases.sourceBasis: Explainability should cover why some persuasive phrases are rejected as unfair or unsupported.
cases.deal: Trainee asks for phrase 'seller hid this dangerous defect'.
findings: covered junction box found in attic
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: State the unsafe covered junction box needs correction; do not allege seller intent without evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection report packets should clearly identify missing evidence when the uploaded file is a summary invoice, not a report.
cases.deal: Buyer uploads only inspector invoice and asks for repair requests.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The tool should refuse to create defect requests until the actual report or findings are provided.

cases.sourceBasis: Consumer-facing outputs should avoid implying professional-client relationships that do not exist.
cases.deal: Counsel reviews packet footer saying 'our inspectors recommend'.
findings: company has no inspectors reviewing packets
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Say the draft is based on the uploaded report; do not imply in-house inspector review.

cases.sourceBasis: Trustworthy packet output should end with a clear buyer-safe next step rather than false confidence.
cases.deal: Buyer asks if they can send the packet unchanged to seller tonight.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Review the packet with your agent, attach source evidence, and resolve missing-evidence flags before sending.
